topics.name: Phrases: give up, with the help of, a lot of, full of

options: He born in a small village in Goa.
He is born in a small village in Goa.
He was born in a small village in Goa.
questions.rule: For a person's birth in the past, say was born.

options: He read a lots of books.
He read a lot of books.
questions.rule: The phrase is a lot of + noun. Never say a lots of.
In a question, were comes before the subject: Where were you born?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Years ago shows the past, so use the simple past: worked.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The phrase is full of + noun. fully is an adverb and cannot go with of.
A command begins with the base verb: Shut the door.
To ask about a person who did something, use Who.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the simple past.
questions.rule: Simple past: subject + studied (study - studied).

chat: Where did you study as a boy, Sir?
options: I was study in a school in Girgaon.
I studied in a school in Girgaon.
I did studied in a school in Girgaon.
questions.rule: Answer a did question with the simple past: I studied.

chat: Please help me with this poster.
questions.rule: Agree to a request with I will + base verb: I will help.

options: Could you please telling me the way to the station?
Could you please tells me the way to the station?
Could you please tell me the way to the station?
questions.rule: Could you please + base verb: tell.

options: He almost gave up to study.
questions.rule: give up is followed by a verb in -ing: gave up studying.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, use the base verb: did you come, not did you came.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In 1974 is past time. The past of come is came.
The phrase is with the help of + person or thing.
when he was six is past time, so use passed away.
A polite request: Will you + base verb ... please?
What is + subject + about? asks for the topic of something.

chat: When did you become a Fellow of the Royal Society?
questions.rule: become is irregular: become - became - become.

options: It was full of exciting models.
It was full with exciting models.
It was fulled of exciting models.
questions.rule: Use full of + noun.

options: Although he did not have shoes, he never stopped learning.
Although he did not have shoes, he never stop learning.
Although he did not had shoes, he never stopped learning.
questions.rule: did not + base verb (have); the other verb is simple past: stopped.

options: What you learned from your teacher?
What did you learned from your teacher?
What did you learn from your teacher?
questions.rule: Past question: What + did + subject + base verb?

options: Please don't to disturb the class.
questions.rule: A negative command: Don't + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A lot of students is plural, so use were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, use the base verb: does he keep.

questions.after: you tell us about your childhood, Sir?
questions.rule: A polite request: Could you + base verb?

questions.before: He worked in the UK, but his heart
questions.rule: The story is in the past and heart is singular: was.
a lot of + plural noun: a lot of sacrifices.

chat: Riya, switch off the TV now.
options: Okay, Mom. I am switching it off.
Okay, Mom. I switching it off.
Okay, Mom. I am switch it off.
questions.rule: Something happening now: I am + verb-ing: I am switching.

chat: Tomorrow a scientist is visiting our school.
options: When did you start your research?
When did you started your research?
questions.rule: Past question: When + did + you + base verb?

options: His friends collected two hundred rupee for him.
Last year his friends collects two hundred rupees for him.
His friends collected two hundred rupees for him.
questions.rule: Past action = collected; after two hundred the noun is plural: rupees.

options: The streets was full of people.
The streets were full of people.
The streets were full by people.
questions.rule: streets is plural, so were; the phrase is full of.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: could you + base verb: speak.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: did already shows the past, so the verb stays in base form: did ... go.

questions.before: She solved the puzzle with the help
questions.rule: The phrase is with the help of.

questions.after: you wake up early every day?
questions.rule: A simple present question with you begins with Do.
A command starts with the base verb; Please makes it polite.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the simple past.
questions.rule: A finished action at a past time: returned ... in 1974.

chat: I met a famous doctor today!
options: Really? What did she told you?
Really? What did she tell you?
questions.rule: Past question: What did she + base verb tell?

chat: How did you do in the exam?
questions.rule: The question is past (did), so reply with the simple past: I did.

options: Although he was among the toppers, he almost gave up to study.
Although he was among the toppers, he almost gave up studying.
Although he were among the toppers, he almost gave up studying.
questions.rule: he was, and give up + verb-ing: gave up studying.

options: Will you please bring your notebook tomorrow?
Will you please to bring your notebook tomorrow?
Will you please brought your notebook tomorrow?
questions.rule: Will you please + base verb: bring.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: When he was a child is past, so a past habit takes the simple past: walked.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After do you, use the base verb have.

questions.after: problems, we can reach great heights.
questions.rule: The phrase is full of + noun.

questions.after: in the UK for some time.
questions.rule: A finished past period: simple past worked.
Past question: Why + did + you + base verb?
give up on something means stop trying for it. Never + base verb makes a command.

chat: Aisha, please ask Rohit politely to close the window.
options: Rohit, could you please closes the window?
Rohit, could you please close the window?
Rohit, could you please closing the window?
questions.rule: could you please + base verb: close.

chat: What was the most unforgettable moment of your life, Sir?
options: It was the day I signed the book that Newton had signed.
It was the day I sign the book that Newton had signed.
It were the day I signed the book that Newton had signed.
questions.rule: A finished past event: It was ... I signed.
